prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: a local concept presentation for Concert of Europe, a grand strategy game set 1836–1918. Design ONE coherent identity concept, THE CONGRESS TABLE. Historically grounded in the five-power diplomatic system following the Congress of Vienna: Austria, Britain, Prussia, Russia, France. This is an original contemporary game identity, not a reproduction of an official historical insignia.
Create an elegant landscape identity proof on solid charcoal #12161b. Main area: a distinctive flat brass #c9a45c emblem of a small oval congress table viewed from above, exactly five clearly separated period chair backs around it, and a folded ivory treaty/map on the tabletop. The five seats must be legible, deliberately asymmetrical spacing suitable for diplomacy rather than a flower, no people. A restrained engraved outline style with strong silhouette, vector-friendly, no texture or 3D. Under it place the exact title "Concert of Europe" in generous antique literary small-cap serif typography inspired by IM Fell English SC. Small line "1836–1918". Bottom third separated by a fine brass rule: show a compact top-menu horizontal lockup of the SAME emblem next to "Concert of Europe", and a simplified icon in a small dark square for favicon, plus a tiny actual-scale icon. The small emblem should reduce to table + five seats without treaty detail. Small label at top left "01 / THE CONGRESS TABLE". Thoughtful whitespace, polished typographic proportions, usable game branding. No laurel, musical instruments, notes, modern EU stars, single national eagle, weapons, gradients, photorealism or unnecessary ornament. Render only this one design, not alternatives.

Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: a local concept presentation for Concert of Europe, a grand strategy game set 1836–1918. Design ONE coherent identity concept, THE FIVE SEALS. Historically inspired by treaties and the five-power diplomatic system following the Congress of Vienna: Austria, Britain, Prussia, Russia, France. Original game identity, not an authentic historical insignia.
Landscape identity proof on solid charcoal #12161b. Main area: a compact icon of an ivory folded treaty document with a strong decorative brass top rule, exactly FIVE circular brass diplomatic seals hanging on short ribbons from its lower edge, at subtly stepped heights, strong elegant geometry. Each seal a simple embossed dot or abstract mark; no fabricated national arms. Period engraved character, brass #c9a45c and ivory #e8e3d7, flat vector-friendly forms, no distressed texture. Make the whole document and five pendants form a memorable readable silhouette. Beneath put exact title "Concert of Europe" in antique literary small-cap serif inspired by IM Fell English SC, plus "1836–1918". Bottom third separated by a fine brass rule: a top-menu horizontal lockup of the SAME symbol beside "Concert of Europe", and a simplified favicon in a small charcoal square, plus tiny actual-scale icon. The favicon keeps document and five seals with heavier strokes and no internal writing. Top-left label "02 / THE FIVE SEALS". Rich period dignity, careful whitespace and precise typography. No laurels, musical notes, EU stars, weapons, crown floating above everything, mock photographs, gradients, 3D, extra concepts. Render only this one design.

Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: a local concept presentation for Concert of Europe, a grand strategy game set 1836–1918. Design ONE coherent identity concept, THE PENTARCHY. Inspired by the five great powers Britain, Austria, Prussia, Russia and France in the historical Concert of Europe, their heraldic diplomacy and division of influence. Original symbolic game identity, not an authentic historic seal.
Landscape proof on solid charcoal #12161b. Main emblem: exactly FIVE compact pointed heraldic escutcheons, equal size, arranged around a central very simplified silhouette of continental Europe. Shields face upright and sit at top, upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right, as an open heraldic congress composition, with generous breathing room. Use brass #c9a45c outlines and ivory #e8e3d7 European silhouette. Shields have simple differing heraldic divisions only (pale, fess, cross, chevron, plain); these are abstract devices, not claimed authentic national arms. Engraved late-Georgian bookplate aesthetic, clean enough to redraw in SVG, flat colors, beautifully balanced negative space. No enclosing star, floral or gear appearance. Under emblem exact title "Concert of Europe" in antique literary small-cap serif typography inspired by IM Fell English SC; smaller "1836–1918". Bottom third separated by a thin rule: compact top-menu horizontal version beside "Concert of Europe", and simplified favicon in a small dark square plus tiny actual-scale proof; favicon reduces to five shield silhouettes around a central dot with no map detail. Top left label "03 / THE PENTARCHY". No laurel, music, modern EU imagery, weapons, photorealism, 3D or gradients. One design only.
